business_problem: Food Ladder needed to scale greenhouse onboarding, school support and curriculum creation for hundreds of remote schools without relying on staff travel and manual lesson preparation, while preserving the personal guidance that defined the nonprofit's work.
solution_summary: Food Ladder worked with IBM Client Engineering to turn manual education and support workflows into an AI-powered operating model built on IBM watsonx.ai, IBM watsonx Assistant and IBM Granite models. The team first streamlined service requests so teachers could submit requests digitally instead of through after-hours phone calls and paperwork. IBM then built a chat agent to guide schools through greenhouse onboarding and answer common questions after equipment arrived, reducing staff intervention. For curriculum work, the team tested multiple large language models before selecting Granite because it stayed consistent with source material and context when generating unit plans, lesson plans and remixed content. That gave Food Ladder one AI stack for intake, teacher self-service and educational-content generation, helping the organization move from a hand-crafted support model to a much more scalable platform for school operations and learning.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Supports the AI workflows Food Ladder uses for request automation, onboarding assistance and educational-content generation.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx Assistant
solution_components.role: Provides the conversational agent that guides teachers through onboarding and routine support tasks.

solution_components.name: IBM Granite
solution_components.role: Generates lesson plans and remixed educational materials while staying aligned to source content and curriculum context.

data_flow: Teacher requests and onboarding questions enter digital workflows backed by watsonx Assistant, while curriculum inputs and remix requests are processed by Granite and watsonx.ai to generate classroom materials and guidance for schools using Food Ladder greenhouses.
business_outcome: Food Ladder gave teachers and staff time back, improved the school experience, and created a scalable model that supports its plan to grow from tens of schools to a global network of AI-enabled food-production hubs.
metrics: Expects to scale from 132,480 meals in 2024 to 25 million meals in 2030
architecture_clues: IBM built the initial solution in approximately two and a half months.
Food Ladder tested several LLMs before selecting Granite for lesson-plan generation.
The organization uses one watsonx-based stack across request intake, onboarding and content creation.

"produce more than 25 million meals annually by 2030"
